findings: Merge conflict in FinalizeFilters (physical_hash_join.cpp): the bloom filter is pushed only when there is no cast, no storage_offset and join_condition[filter_idx]==0. This is correct. The multi-key BF is built in JoinHashTable::Finalize from VectorOperations::Hash of the gathered first key column (condition_types[0]), so the probe side's hash of an un-cast, un-shifted column matches it. Single-key HTs still insert in InsertHashes, so no key is inserted twice.

CastJoinFilterValueToStorage: computes storage = key + offset in HUGEINT with TryAdd. It returns false on overflow or a failed cast, and the caller then skips the filter. NULL is left as is and the existing IsNull check skips it. Every consumer of storage_type (the min/max filter and the IN/range filters) goes through this helper, so no pushed filter can use a value without the offset applied.

Range-set path in PushInFilter: in_list is unique (built from a set) and IsDenseRange has already sorted it for integral non-UHUGEINT types. The type equality check and the IsIntegral/UHUGEINT guard keep it consistent. gaps.size() >= max_filter_count > split_count, so nth_element stays in bounds. The ranges cover every key, and the result is wrapped in an OptionalFilter (zonemap only), so a filter that is too broad can never drop rows. The extra cost is limited to scanning at most 64x the dynamic_or_filter_threshold keys.

Optimizer pushdown through __internal_compress_integral_*: it takes only one offset level, requires a constant non-NULL offset and a source type no wider than 64 bits, and carries the offset through set-operation children. These are general rules based on the plan's shape.

Cardinality changes (SEMI denominator from tdom/RHS cardinality, an extra cut for HAVING-style range predicates on aggregate results with a floor of 1, and 0.05 selectivity for LIKE/contains filters) only affect estimates and cannot change results. They key on expression shape and function class, never on names or literals.
The prefetch code in join_hashtable.cpp depends on a size threshold (a 4MB pointer table) and does not affect correctness.
Nothing in the diff refers to tables, columns, literals or dataset sizes, and it does not touch timing, settings defaults or tests.
